data.text: Operator 2026-10-23 answers to the graded-policies questions (GP-decide): Q1 five-word scale (info, recommended, best-practice, required, forbidden): YES. Q2 a best-practice item must be answered (comply or explain) before complete: YES. Q3 at-least-k-of-n alternatives in the first cut: YES. Q4 can a project add an alternative to a company any-of: the operator chose YES (NOT the recommended no). Q5 new company policy audits one release first: YES. Q6/Q7: 90-day waiver cap; tier 2 approval for project waivers, tier 3 for company exceptions to a locked policy; opt-out per item or per project with review_by up to 180 days (recommended). Q8 one merged charter knob: YES. Q9 MCP actions: in the ONE record family (per D-mcp-new-nouns), not the rule family. Q10 commit signing (gpg/ssh/gitsign) as the first any-of example: YES. Q11 severity label: later. Also: the operator confirmed KEEPING D-audit-calls-2026-10-10 and D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted (no change).

data.alternatives: Three words plus default-on flag (kept only as fallback). Free-form per-company levels (rejected: no common meaning across packs).
data.consequences: One fixed vocabulary across rules, requirements, principles and org policy; the six existing vocabularies map onto it as a view (GP-inventory pins them first). Risk: operators find five words confusing; fallback is three words plus a default-on flag (invalidation 3 in the proposal).
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: YES. The strength scale is exactly five words: info, recommended, best-practice, required, forbidden. forbidden is required with negative polarity.
data.title: Graded policies: five-word strength scale
